verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents a public REST API with an API reference that covers 'anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI'. It uses token-based API keys and bot tokens, offers a read-only endpoint, and has an OpenAPI 3.0.1 spec in the official MCP repository. The probe's 404s at guessed docs-domain OpenAPI paths only mean the spec lives elsewhere; they do not contradict the API's existence. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of driving the API end-to-end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
FireHydrant allows you to access the API with an API key using token-based authentication.
FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account.
publishes a FireHydrant OpenAPI document (.speakeasy/openapi.output.yaml): openapi "3.0.1"
